artifacts.summary: Confirms the single unsafe source-store mutation site (test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's regression-anchor check), recommends a reorder fix (mutate the already-copied $SUT, not $CORE_DIR, eliminating both the EXIT-trap and shared-tree-exposure holes with no new harness infrastructure), finds two existing safe-pattern precedents in the same corpus, audits scripts/tests/ for other sites (none found), verifies an anchored-regex self-exclusion for a paired mechanical detector, and documents the gate-registration conventions (verify-deploy.sh gate28_run + gate-registry.data row) for that detector.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/, test suites that sandbox-copy source-store scripts into $WORKDIR (via a per-file setup_sandbox()) already execute the sandboxed copy ($SUT), not the real source-store file ($CORE_DIR), in run_sut. A 'deliberately break X, confirm red, then revert' regression-anchor fixture should therefore mutate $SUT AFTER calling setup_sandbox(), never $CORE_DIR before it -- this closes the shared-working-tree exposure window outright (no concurrent reader can ever observe the mutation) and makes EXIT-trap-based backup/restore unnecessary, since the mutated copy is naturally wiped by the next setup_sandbox() call. Two precedents already use this safe shape: test-git-commit-scoped.sh's X1/X2 inversion probes and test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh's self-test, both via a mktemp -d scratch copy.

agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/test-harness-lib.sh does not exist in this repo despite being a plausible-sounding name; setup_sandbox is defined independently per-test-file (34+ files each define their own copy-from-$CORE_DIR-into-$WORKDIR logic). Before assuming a shared test-harness library exists and planning to extend it, grep for the actual function definitions first.

An anchored-start regex (^[[:space:]]*while false[[:space:]]*&&) correctly distinguishes a real code-level 'while false &&' anti-pattern guard from a test file's own sed replacement-string text that legitimately contains the same phrase as a quoted argument (e.g. sed -i "s/.../while false \&\& .../"). The sed line's actual text begins with 'sed -i', not 'while false &&', so a line-start anchor avoids the false positive without needing a blanket path exclusion.
